messages:
toni: Heads-up: canary for kestrel-mix-int8 showing fragmented funcall outputs when prompts contain code-mixed snippets (EN + local variable names). Started after last PTQ pass.
canary-bot: canary=kestrel-mix-int8 subset=code-mix parse_fail_rate=0.7% -> 5.4% (24h)
rebecca: ugh. examples?
chen: dropping a few excerpts from raw model text (sanitized):
```
{"tool": "saveDoc", "args": {"path": "/tmp/notes.md", "content": "Meeting: discussion sobre usuario_id=1234"}}
{"tool": "guardar_documento", "args": {"ruta": "/tmp/notes.md", "contenido": "Meeting: user_id=1234"}}
{"tool":"saveDoc","args":"{\"path\":\"/tmp/log.txt\",\"content\":\"Nota: última línea:\u201d}"}
{"tool": "saveDoc", "args": ["/tmp/x.txt", "contenido"]}
```
chen: patterns: 1) camelCase tool vs translated tool, 2) localized key names (ruta/contenido), 3) args sometimes serialized as a string (escaped JSON), 4) args as array positionally.
laura: does this correlate with prompt tokenization? like variable names glued to punctuation?
toni: yes - code-mixed prompts where users include inline identifiers or variable-like tokens seem hit more. short prompts amplify the effect.
marco: baseline fp16 vs int8 numbers?
toni: fp16 parse_fail ~0.6% int8 ~5.4% on the same set; big jump.
rebecca: could be quant causing subtoken merges that favor localized words or small id tokens. similar to earlier cross-lang cases but now code-mix introduces token boundaries near punctuation/underscores.
laura: quick mitigation options: 1) prompt-side: inject a short canonical English example always (few-token anchor) to bias key names; 2) postprocessing heuristics: alias map (guardar_documento->saveDoc), unescape args-as-string, single->double quote normalize, array->object coercer; 3) PTQ ablation: preserve bias for identifier tokens, or re-run with different per-token clipping.
chen: I prototyped a tiny alias map + unescape step in the canary postprocessor. On a 2k-sample slice it recovered ~78% of failures and introduced ~0.3% mis-coercions (rare wrong-tool). Cheap latency.
rebecca: nice. cost tradeoff: repair means extra CPU + some latency, but it avoids falling back to heavier model. we should measure p50/p95 latency delta.
marco: also thinking of a lightweight classifier pre-invoke: check token histogram of model output for non-ASCII / quotes / bracket mismatch; only run repair if flagged. that reduces wasted repair cycles.
laura: agree. also add telemetry dimensions: failure_type = [localized_key, args_stringified, positional_args, wrong_enum] so we can prioritize.
toni: action items:
- chen: run 10k-sample ablation across mixes (en+es, en+zh, en+ja) comparing fp16, int8, int8+postproc. include latency bucketing. owner: chen. (48h)
- laura: add fine-grained parse_failure_type metrics to canary dashboard. owner: laura. (24h)
- rebecca: coordinate with quant team to trial PTQ with "identifier-preserve" seed and higher clip for punctuation/subtokens. owner: rebecca. (72h)
- marco: build quick classifier heuristic and wire to canary pipeline to gate postproc. owner: marco. (48h)
chen: also logging detail: flag samples where alias_map changed the tool so we can audit false-positive conversions.
rebecca: if postproc doesn't recover >=90% with low mis-coercion, we keep code-mix endpoints on fp16 until quant fixes.
toni: thanks all. this one feels subtle but manageable. ping here with results. :mag:
